rationale: I went and looked at the thing. shots/mgr100a-wide.png, seed 42, day 6, 14:43, a clear midsummer afternoon: the town above the lane is dense and finished, and the bottom of the picture is a BLACK RECTANGLE. It is not a rendering bug, it is an omission with a comment on it - buildGrid's last clause reads `// below the lane: our own building, with the river slipping between its two halves` and then sets rows 79..87 to VOID, and drawGround's first line is `if (t === WALL || t === VOID) continue`. So 1107 cells, 9.1% of the grid, the NEAREST rows and therefore the largest ones on screen, have never been painted by anything. Measured on HEAD: on a 1600x950 desktop the band runs from project(60,79,0)[1] = 676.4 to sillTop() = 794.6 of a canvas H = 859 - 13.8% of the picture; on a 390x844 phone it is 536.2 to 700.5 of H = 757.25, 21.7%. That is the answer to 'what would most change a thirty-second look', and it is a SPATIAL answer, which is what this batch needs: mapFlat is two iterations from firing, the map has not moved since #87, and `structures` and `passages` have not moved once in the whole run. So this batch is RUNG 4b, and b100 is the bet: give the diorama its foreground. The rest balance the grid and are aimed at what the same screenshot shows: an evenly-lit town under a sky whose eleven cloud banks cast nothing on it (b102, Sky 11 back, and drawClouds is a sky-strip-only pass - grepped, confirmed), an evening that does not end (b101, People 10 back, c137: a dusk stayer is still walking the plaza at 03h on four seeds), a plaza whose paving is 400 identical setts (b103, Plaza 7 back, New CA, and `moss`/`weed`/`lichen` appear nowhere in the source), and one measured polish (b104, Street 6 back). Cost discipline, third pass running: every number a brief needs is IN the brief, and where I could not price something I have said so rather than inventing a target.
